note: Frozen evaluation set, append-only on the same terms as questions.json: add questions, never reword one, because a reworded question silently invalidates every earlier recording that used it (D-088).
why: O-16 asks what a corpus costs once it stops refreshing. That effect can only appear where new papers actually arrive, so the set is split into a fast arm and a slow control arm, chosen by MEASURED arXiv submissions in the 30 days to 2026-09-25 (tests/eval/velocity.py). Testing staleness only on mature topics would be underpowered by construction -- D-095's mistake, pointed the other way.
falsifies: If the fast arm shows no quality or recency difference after months of drift, staleness is not a real cost on this workload and O-16 closes as 'report only' permanently rather than provisionally. If the SLOW arm shows a difference, the measurement is broken, not the corpus: those topics gained ~0 papers.
protocol: See docs/staleness-experiment.md. The comparison runs in the FUTURE against the corpus seeded today; nothing is recorded now.
velocity_note: submissions matching the topic terms in the 30 days to 2026-09-25, from arXiv's own opensearch:totalResults. Recorded so the arm split can be defended later without re-measuring, and so drift in these numbers is itself visible.
